Joint distribution: First metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint (podagra) most common; also ankles, knees, elbows, wrists, fingers, and the ear helix. — Lower temperature in distal joints favors crystal precipitation; mechanical stress and reduced blood flow promote nucleation.
A 48‑year‑old male farmer presents with a 2‑day history of sudden, excruciating pain in the right first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint.
A 55-year-old obese man develops sudden onset of severe pain, redness and swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

qs.q: A 60-year-old man experiences excruciating pain, erythema, and swelling in the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Arthrocentesis reveals negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals. What initiated crystal formation?
o: Supersaturation of urate in the synovial fluid
Precipitation of basic calcium apatite deposits
qs.e: Gout occurs when monosodium urate crystals precipitate in joints due to hyperuricemia and supersaturation of synovial fluid.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: Internal Medicine Exam - October 24, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 50-year-old man with chronic hyperuricemia experiences a sudden, exquisitely painful attack of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. What is the initial molecular event following MSU crystal phagocytosis by synovial macrophages?
qs.e: When MSU crystals are phagocytosed by macrophages, they activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, leading to the release of IL-1β and subsequent intense neutrophilic inflammation. Xanthine oxidase is involved in purine catabolism and hyperuricemia, not the downstream inflammatory cascade.
qs.s: Infectious Arthritis: Bacterial, TB & Viral Joint Infections: MCQs

qs.q: A 54-year-old man presents with a severely painful, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint that developed overnight. Synovial fluid analysis reveals needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. Which cellular process directly triggers the acute inflammatory response in this joint?
o: Phagocytosis of precipitated monosodium urate crystals by polymorphonuclear neutrophils
Autoimmune-mediated proliferation of synovial lining cells with immune complex deposition
Deposition of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals within the articular cartilage
Direct bacterial invasion of the synovial space following minor soft tissue trauma
qs.e: Acute gout flares are driven by neutrophils phagocytosing monosodium urate crystals, which triggers inflammasome activation and cytokine release. Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystal deposition causes pseudogout rather than classic acute gout.

qs.q: A 45-year-old man presents with acute, severe pain, swelling, and erythema of the first metatarsophalangeal joint of his right foot that woke him up at night. What is this classic manifestation called?
o: Gonagra affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint
Tophi affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint
Chiragra affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint
Podagra affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint
qs.e: Podagra refers to inflammation of the MTP joint of the big toe, which is the most common site for acute gouty arthritis. Gonagra and chiragra refer to knee and finger joint inflammation, respectively.

qs.q: A 64-year-old man with a 15-year history of poorly controlled hyperuricemia presents with firm, painless, yellowish-white nodules over his left olecranon bursa and first metatarsophalangeal joints. What is the underlying histological composition of these lesions?
o: Aggregates of monosodium urate crystals surrounded by chronic inflammatory cells
Necrotic adipocytes enclosed within a thick fibrous connective tissue capsule
Dystrophic calcium phosphate deposits within damaged tendon insertions
Proliferating synovial lining cells mixed with acute neutrophilic infiltrate
qs.e: Tophi consist of dense aggregates of monosodium urate crystals surrounded by macrophages, lymphocytes, and foreign-body giant cells. They are distinct from lipomas, purulent abscesses, or pure calcium deposits.

qs.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a hot, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint. Arthrocentesis is attempted twice by different clinicians, but insufficient synovial fluid is obtained for crystal analysis. Which diagnostic imaging modality is best indicated next?
qs.e: Ultrasound is the preferred non-invasive imaging modality to evaluate for the double-contour sign and tophi when joint fluid cannot be obtained. Scintigraphy and MRI lack the specific spatial resolution required for crystal identification.

qs.q: A 60-year-old man presents with severe pain in his first metatarsophalangeal joint. Joint aspiration reveals crystals that appear needle-shaped and show negative birefringence under polarized light. What is the primary chemical composition of these crystals?
qs.e: Gout is caused by monosodium urate crystals, which are needle-shaped and negatively birefringent. In contrast, pseudogout involves calcium pyrophosphate crystals that are rhomboid-shaped and positively birefringent.
qs.s: Bone & Soft Tissue Tumour Pathology: Must-Know Diagnoses — CAT: MCQs

qs.q: A 48-year-old man has severe pain, swelling, and tenderness in his left first metatarsophalangeal joint. Joint aspiration shows neutrophils and needle-shaped crystals. His acute response is most likely mediated through crystal-induced NOD-like receptor signaling of which of the following?
qs.e: Needle-shaped (sodium urate) crystals in the joint = acute gout. Crystals activate NOD-like receptors → inflammasome assembly → caspase-1 activation → cleavage of pro-IL-1β to active IL-1β → acute inflammatory arthritis.
